title: Proton Beam Radiotherapy
description: Medicare coverage criteria for proton beam radiotherapy. Covered for indications requiring steep dose falloff to spare critical dose-limiting organs: chordomas and chondrosarcomas of skull base or spine, ocular melanomas, primary CNS tumors in close proximity to brainstem/optic chiasm, or re-irradiation.

criteria.name: Skull Base, Spine Chordoma, or Critical Structure Proximity
criteria.description: Histologically confirmed skull base/cervical chordoma, chondrosarcoma, ocular melanoma, or CNS tumor abutting critical dose-limiting neural and ocular structures (optic chiasm, optic nerve, brainstem, spinal cord, retina, cochlea). Note: Instance list is author-defined from policy indications; source status is MISMATCH/unverified.
criteria.clinical_intent: Validate anatomical and dosimetric justification for Bragg peak physics abutting class of critical neural structures
criteria.source_text_excerpt: Benign or malignant conditions otherwise not suitable for intensity modulated radiation therapy (IMRT) or 3- dimensional conformal therapy involving the base of the skull or axial skeleton, including but not limited to chordomas and chondrosarcomas.

criteria.name: Comparative Dosimetric Treatment Plan Demonstrating Sparing
criteria.description: Comparative dosimetric planning demonstrating that conventional photon IMRT cannot deliver target curative dose without exceeding normal tissue tolerance.
criteria.clinical_intent: Objective dosimetric proof of photon inadequacy
criteria.source_text_excerpt: Specifically, the record must address the lower risk to normal tissue, the lower risk of disease recurrence, and the advantages of the treatment over IMRT or 3-dimensional conformal Dosimetric evidence of reduced normal tissue toxicity and/or improved tumor control must be maintained.

criteria.name: Widespread Distant Metastases Exclusion
criteria.description: Patients with widespread systemic metastatic disease or terminal prognosis where focal proton curative intent cannot be achieved.
criteria.source_text_excerpt: In general, proton beam radiotherapy is not indicated for cancers that are widely disseminated, such as leukemias, have hematogenous metastases or as a short-term palliative procedure.
